rationale: The fixed experiment b8fa9bc20e164089beff30308ce68220-experiment has been executed and retained, so this update converts the Node API probe into an execution-grounded conclusion for question b8fa9bc20e164089beff30308ce68220-question-0 and records the observed instance as durable knowledge: the member control returned immediately with no error, while the same Node.Propose call after the node applied its own removal blocked for the full caller timeout and returned only 'context deadline exceeded' with the node confirmed outside the configuration. The question is marked explained with the sourced behaviour entry as its premise, and the deliberate nature of the block, the caller-supplied context and the unmeasured non-expiring-context case stay in the counterevidence and limitations.

knowledge.assertion: The proposal channel is disabled when the node applies its own removal, so the call can only complete on the caller's context, which is what the execution observed.

knowledge.statement: In the retained execution of the fixed experiment (three-voter cluster {1,2,3}; node 1 a bare raft leader at term 1 with committed 1, node 2 a bare follower, node 3 driven through the Node API as a follower; fault-free in-process delivery; caller timeout 200 ms), Node.Propose on node 3 while it was still a member returned no error in 0 ms (parsed index 1: error_text '<nil>', elapsed_ms 0, blocked_until_deadline false, node3_in_config true). After a ConfChangeV2 removing node 3 was proposed on the leader and applied on node 3 through the Node API, node 3 was absent from the configuration with voters [1,2] (index 2: node3_in_config false, node3_lead 1, node3_state StateFollower, committed 3), and the same Node.Propose call then blocked for 201 ms and returned only the caller's context error (index 3: error_text 'context deadline exceeded', elapsed_ms 201, timeout_ms 200, blocked_until_deadline true).
knowledge.conditions: One executed in-process experiment with the fixed harness bytes of experiment b8fa9bc20e164089beff30308ce68220-experiment (receipt d5f37430774c4bbd9d64967e3f82290d, exit 0, changed_target_files [], no parsing errors); the subject node was driven through the Node API with its own Ready/Advance loop, the other voters were bare raft instances, the caller used a 200 ms context, and no restart, snapshot, leadership change or packet loss occurred. One observed instance under these conditions, not a universal guarantee.

interpretations.rationale: Receipt d5f37430774c4bbd9d64967e3f82290d is a completed execution of this investigation's own experiment (status completed, exit 0, outcome tests_passed, unchanged target files, no parsing errors, 4 parsed events). Comparison 0 declares that after the node applied its own removal a proposal through the Node API is reported as not admissible instead of blocking until the caller's deadline; it is violated with a complete valid witness at parsed index 3, correlated to its own admission at index 2 (self_removal_applied for probe_id 'removed': node3_in_config false, voters [1,2], node3_lead 1, node3_state StateFollower, committed 3). The measured operands at index 3 are error_text 'context deadline exceeded', elapsed_ms 201 with timeout_ms 200, blocked_until_deadline true and node3_in_config false, so the call consumed the entire caller timeout and returned only the caller's own context error, carrying no statement that the node is no longer a member. Comparison 1 is the control with identical sampling and holds at index 1, correlated to its admission at index 0 (node_setup for probe_id 'member': leader 1, term 1, committed 1, node3_in_config true, caller timeout 200 ms): the same call returned no error in 0 ms while the node was a member, which shows the call, the timeout, the Node loop and the transport in the harness are functional and that the blocking behaviour depends on the applied removal. The mechanism is the sourced one: node.run disables the proposal channel when the node applies a configuration that no longer contains it (node.go:405-433, with the comment that this 'isn't very sound and likely has bugs' about re-enabling it on leadership change), and Node.Propose's wait path selects only on that channel, ctx.Done or n.done (node.go:513-537), so the library's own statement about admissibility on the proposal path (raft.go:1290-1295, the drop it returns when the removed node is the leader) is never produced here. Engineering significance: the predicate is about the signal a caller receives, and the observed value is that the only signal is the caller's own deadline, which a service using a non-expiring context would never receive, in which case the call would block for the lifetime of the node; that stronger case is recorded as unmeasured rather than observed.

knowledge.assertion: The disabled proposal channel is the reason the call can only complete on the caller's context, which is seen as elapsed 201 ms with the context error at index 3.

counterevidence: The block is deliberate in the captured source: node.run states that it blocks incoming proposals when the node was removed, so a reviewer may read the blocking behaviour as the intended mechanism rather than an implementation error.

The caller can bound the call: Node.Propose takes a context, and with a deadline it returns that deadline error, which is what the witness shows; only a caller that passes a non-expiring context would block indefinitely, and that case was not measured.

The raft layer does produce a drop statement on the proposal path when the removed node is the leader (raft.go:1290-1295), so the finding is about the Node layer's silence rather than about the library never signalling drops.
The control at index 1 shows the same call on the same node works normally while it is a member, which excludes a harness or transport failure as the cause.
Only the subject node applied the removal in this execution; the other voters were driven as bare raft instances, and the removal was applied through the Node API rather than by a full server loop.
limitations: One executed instance with a 200 ms caller context in one process and fault-free delivery; the observation is bounded to those conditions.
The behaviour with a non-expiring context, with a context cancelled by a server shutdown, and with the node stopped mid-call was not measured.

Only removal of a follower was exercised; removal of the leader takes a different branch (already covered by the earlier removed-leader finding), and joint configurations and learner demotion were not probed.

The embedding service's own proposal timeouts, retries and membership tracking are outside the captured package, so whether this behaviour is a practical hazard there and how it should be classified are left to human review.
interpretations.report_title: 节点被移除后 Node.Propose 只以调用方超时结束：没有“不可受理”的信号
interpretations.report_answer: 在快照代码上，三 voter 集群中把 node 3 交给 Node API 驱动：作为成员时同一 Node.Propose 调用 0ms 返回且 error 为 nil（对照）；在 leader 提议移除 node 3 并由其应用该已提交条目后（voters 变为 [1,2]，node3_in_config=false），同样的调用阻塞整段调用方超时（200ms，实测 201ms），最终只返回 'context deadline exceeded'，没有任何“该提案不可受理”的信息。源码显示 node.run 在节点应用了移除自身的配置后把提案通道置为 nil（node.go:405-433，且注释自称这种处理“isn't very sound and likely has bugs”），而 Node.Propose 的等待路径只能在该通道、调用方 context 或节点停止三者之一完成（node.go:513-537），因此 raft 层在同类情形下会给出的 drop 信号（raft.go:1290-1295，针对被移除的 leader）在这条路径上不会出现。若调用方使用不会到期的 context，调用将一直阻塞而没有任何信号——该更强情形未在本实验中测量；是否构成缺陷需人工结合调用方契约复核。
